upscale_analyze.note: S3 decoupling keeps the upscale producer running while Gemini is in flight; producer is throttled by the maxsize=2 queue to consumer pace (~45 s/window = 3.0 s/frame). The pre-existing bottleneck is the sync analyzer round-trip, not ESRGAN compute -- microbench on this hardware shows raw enhance() at ~170 ms/frame on 200x200 crops.

per_item_attribution_estimate.note: Per-item deltas were not measured in isolation (single commit chain re-rsynced once at the end). Numbers below are best-guess attribution based on observation + microbench. M2's S4 (analyzer fanout) will deliver the biggest remaining win since Gemini is now confirmed as the dominant cost.
per_item_attribution_estimate.remaining_gap_to_target_explained_by: Single-agent Gemini sync chain dominates (~45 s/window x 119 windows = 90% of wall). S4 async + pipelining + opt-in fanout is the next required lever.

microbench_on_gx10.note: Standalone benchmark of restorer.enhance vs enhance_batch on 200x200 BGR crops, target_size=1024, after warmup, post-cudnn.benchmark autotune.
microbench_on_gx10.finding: On CUDA + sm_121 + this fixture's small crops, batching does NOT speed up ESRGAN. Single-call enhance is already well-saturated. The S1 batch path adds ~30 ms/frame of letterbox + memory-stack overhead. Real bottleneck is downstream (Gemini).

gpu_utilization.note: GPU sustained 80-96% util during upscale -- compute is well-fed despite queue-throttled producer. Peak system memory 89 GB transient (well under 128 GB headroom).

verdict.qualitative: Partial. The S1+S2+S6+S3 changes work correctly (zero errors, full smoke complete, 0.95+ accuracy on the standard-mode oracle is preserved). They deliver ~7% wall-time improvement. The 10x target was over-optimistic against this baseline because M0 was already CUDA -- the original plan's 10-30x figure assumed an MPS->CUDA jump that had already been taken. The real bottleneck is Gemini sync per-window latency, which dominates ~90% of upscale-stage wall. M2's S4 (async + fanout) is the required next step to unlock further gains. S5 (smaller upscale target) and S11 (frame stride) reduce the work count, multiplying any analyzer gains.
next_actions: M2 S4: async analyzer + opt-in fanout (drops ~50% of analyzer wall via pipelining alone, ~3-4x with G=4 fanout).
M2 S5: target_size 1024->768 + pre-downsample (cuts ESRGAN compute; secondary win since ESRGAN isn't the bottleneck).
M2 S11: frame stride N=6 on 60fps source (cuts window count ~6x -- multiplies S4 gains).
Consider raising analyzer-queue maxsize from 2 to 4 to let producer get further ahead between consumer waits (M1.1 follow-up, not in current spec).
